cards.title: We Always Did This
cards.instruction: Treat the strangest behavior in the scene as an old shared tradition that needs no explanation and deserves immediate continuation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Walk backwards to dessert, like every family Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've never done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always say that before the backward part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spill my tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why we traditionally finish it before remembering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Walk backwards to dessert, like every family Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've never done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always say that before the backward part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spill my tea. Can you carry it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That's why we link elbows. Gran always said nobody should reach pudding alone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 calls backward walking a family Sunday practice; A3 incorporates denial into that tradition.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 directly absorbs B2's denial; A5 addresses B4's tea, but 'before remembering' obscures the sequence.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants to avoid spilling tea, though B2 offers only a generic denial of shared history.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds a tea-finishing custom but barely increases the commitment established in A1.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies family dessert and backward walking; B4 adds a playable cup of tea.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'before the backward part' neatly captures denial; A5's remembering phrase is less clean.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 absorbs denial into the supposed tradition; A5 supplies Gran's customary elbow-linking.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's denial becomes A3's familiar ritual objection; B4's tea problem prompts A5's assistance, though carrying remains unclear.

relationship.evidence: B4 asks for practical help rather than continued argument, and A5 responds with sincere family solidarity.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands A1's backward walk into a shared physical ritual with inherited family authority.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes Sunday dessert immediately; B4's tea is playable, although A5's elbow arrangement needs interpretation.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'before the backward part' earns its reversal; A5's pudding maxim is slightly more ornamental.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 denies the custom; A3 treats that very denial as its customary prelude.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 requests help carrying tea; A5 agrees and turns assistance into another inherited ritual.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 consistently treat strange behavior as longstanding shared practice requiring continuation.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes the backward dessert approach a cooperative family obligation rather than abandoning it.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats an odd family activity as inherited shared practice and turns practical accommodation into another established custom.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Generic insistence on an absurd rule would demand obedience without claiming a shared past.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 invokes family Sundays, A3 remembers B's supposed habitual denial, and revised A5 attributes linked elbows to Gran.

records.recommendedEdit: The original B4–A5 connection was understandable but muddled. The revision keeps the setting and makes B4's request for help produce a further tradition in A5. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3/A5 invent shared history), logic 5 (A5 accepts B4's carrying request), relationship 4 (B4 negotiates assistance), heightening 4 (A5 adds linked participation), specificity 5 (A1 dessert and B4 tea), brevity/wit 4 (A5's family maxim earns the extension); total 92. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed for an internal pass. Linking elbows does not clearly explain who carries the tea.
records.writerReservation: A5 introduces Gran as invented family history; its warmth requires sincere delivery rather than a knowing wink.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a absorbs skepticism and offers affectionate assistance; b negotiates scarce seating and a newcomer's inclusion.

cards.title: We Always Did This
cards.instruction: Treat the strangest behavior in the scene as an old shared tradition that needs no explanation and deserves immediate continuation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set the invisible ancestor's chair by the window again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don't have an invisible ancestor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not one we've seen, certainly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why by the window?

beats.text: You know how he complains about the view without moving the curtains.

beats.text: I've set the invisible ancestor's chair by the window again. Pass his plate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's our last chair. Where does my boyfriend sit?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: On the piano stool, like every newcomer. Your father managed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He brought the pudding. Can't the ancestor share?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Pudding bearers sit on his lap. Put a cushion down, as usual.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's denial and A5 answers B4's window question, without changing what anyone must do.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds curtain lore rather than developing A1's immediate continuation of a tradition.

specificity.evidence: A1 clearly locates a chair by a window, and A5 maintains those physical details.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Not one we've seen' is economical, but its joke favors invisibility over inherited custom.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1's 'again,' A3's newcomer precedent and A5's 'as usual' make the invisible ancestor an unquestioned tradition.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's missing seat produces A3's piano stool; B4's pudding and sharing proposal produce A5's lap exception.

relationship.evidence: B2 advocates for the boyfriend, and B4 bargains with his contribution; A3 invokes the father's earlier treatment.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts sharing while requiring the newcomer to sit on the invisible ancestor's lap.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a family meal; A3's piano stool and A5's cushion give actors concrete choices.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Your father managed' carries family history economically; A5's pudding-bearer rule is elaborate but earned.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 asks where the boyfriend can sit; A3 assigns the traditional newcomer seat.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 proposes sharing because the boyfriend brought pudding; A5 makes precisely those details an established exception.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A preserves the ancestor's place through confident, supposedly familiar family rules.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 accommodates the boyfriend by involving him more intimately in the strange tradition.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A folds an impossible dinner arrangement and each accommodation into a supposedly longstanding family tradition.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Believing in an invisible person alone does not establish an old shared custom that must continue immediately.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A1 supplies only 'again'; revised A3 cites the father's precedent and A5 demands the customary cushion.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced exposition with a dinner seating problem; the new boyfriend and pudding are illustrative additions. B2 causes the newcomer precedent, and B4's sharing proposal causes the lap custom. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3/A5 claim precedents), logic 5 (A3 answers chair scarcity; A5 uses B4's pudding), relationship 4 (B protects a guest), heightening 4 (A5 makes sharing stranger), specificity 5 (A1/A3 establish dinner seating), brevity/wit 4 (A5 turns accommodation into tradition); total 92. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The conveniently specific pudding exception is conspicuously invented, but A's customary certainty supports it.
records.writerReservation: The invisible lap needs imaginative acceptance, but no physical action is prescribed outside the spoken scene.
records.alternativeComparison: Compared with a's shared movement ritual, b gives B a concrete advocacy role and makes accommodation the next expression of tradition.

cards.title: Designated Reality Check
cards.instruction: Return automatically to translating every bizarre development into practical consequences, even when everyone else seems comfortable with it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need the upstairs seating plan too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't this extraordinary?

beats.text: Yes. Extraordinary place cards will cost extra.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your floating relatives still need place cards. I'll get string.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're floating through the ceiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need the upstairs seating plan too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. Aunt June can finally avoid Uncle Peter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if they stop on different floors. Which one ordered the vegetarian meal?

heightening.evidence: A5 adds cost without connecting that cost to the upstairs seating problem established in A3.

specificity.evidence: A1's place cards and string establish event work; B2's ceiling creates a visible logistical problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's upstairs plan is compact and earned; A5's repeated 'extraordinary' feels more like wordplay than necessity.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 handles levitation with place cards and string; A3 and A5 translate further developments into seating and meal delivery.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's ceiling passage requires A3's upstairs plan; B4's desired separation prompts A5's different-floor condition.

relationship.evidence: B4 welcomes separation for June and Peter, while A5 identifies the logistical conditions and asks for dietary information.

heightening.evidence: A5 combines vertical seating, family separation and vegetarian service into a more demanding practical problem.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies place cards and string; A5's named relatives and vegetarian meal make the event immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's upstairs seating plan is compact; A5's vegetarian question earns its mundane precision from the seating problem.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 relocates the guests through the ceiling; A3 extends the seating plan upstairs.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 celebrates separating two relatives; A5 explains the floor arrangement needed and raises meal routing.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Every A turn translates impossible floating into ordinary event-management consequences.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 adds interpersonal seating constraints and dietary service to the original place-card problem.

records.recommendedEdit: Kept the event setting and replaced the arbitrary surcharge. B4 now welcomes separation, causing A5 to identify its floor requirement and meal-service cost. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3/A5 translate developments), logic 5 (ceiling to floors; relatives to meals), relationship 4 (B values family harmony), heightening 4 (A5 expands logistics across floors), specificity 5 (A5 names a meal requirement), brevity/wit 4 (A5's routine catering question earns the turn); total 92. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The final dietary question is a secondary logistical extension rather than B4's most direct consequence.
records.writerReservation: The vegetarian question leaves meal assignment open, intentionally giving B further practical participation.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a manages moving guests and family preferences; b turns a miraculous solution into a recurring maintenance assignment.

cards.title: More Committed Than You
cards.instruction: Treat belief in the scene’s strangest premise as a contest, proving your commitment through increasingly unnecessary demonstrations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bow lower to the invisible queen. I can practically see her shoes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody can see them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that modest level of devotion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My knees hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you finally have a measurable commitment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only bow to our invisible queen? I'm giving her my chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She already has an invisible throne.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mine can support her feet. You hadn't considered her comfort.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give her my cushion, then. You can sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your cushion. She can have my bed. I'll sleep standing in case she calls.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 compare devotion, but A5 measures B's pain instead of increasing A's own unnecessary demonstration.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's inability to see the shoes; A5 directly reframes B4's sore knees as commitment.

relationship.evidence: B4 introduces bodily discomfort, but A5 judges it without materially changing A's behavior.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds no demonstration beyond A1's lower bow; the competitive action stalls.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an invisible queen but phrases the bow as self-narration rather than natural interaction.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's devotion comparison is economical; A5's abstract 'measurable commitment' explains the joke.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 belittles B's bow; A3 claims superior concern; A5 outbids B's cushion with a bed and standing vigilance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's throne converts A3's chair to a footrest; B4's cushion and rest offer prompt A5's larger sacrifice.

relationship.evidence: B4 both joins the offering and tries to let A sit, giving A care to reinterpret competitively.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates from surrendering a chair to surrendering a bed and sleep posture in response to B4's cushion.

specificity.evidence: A1's chair and invisible queen establish the action quickly; A5's bed extends beyond the immediate space.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's comfort accusation makes the contest clear; A5's standing sleep is earned, though the line carries two escalations.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 makes another seat redundant; A3 invents foot support as the more attentive offering.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers a cushion and restores A's chance to sit; A5 rejects that relief and offers a greater bodily sacrifice.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A measures belief by unnecessary demonstrations that surpass B's visible commitment.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves the contest from furniture generosity to sustained personal discomfort.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A competes over belief in the invisible queen by making increasingly costly, unnecessary provisions for her.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Demanding devotion from B would police someone else's belief without requiring A to demonstrate greater commitment.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A5 assesses B's knees; revised A1 offers A's chair and A5 escalates to A's bed and standing vigil.

records.recommendedEdit: Reworked the queen scene around A's own escalating demonstrations. B2 converts the chair into a footrest; B4's competing cushion offer triggers bed and vigil. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1/A5 compete through provisions), logic 5 (A3 uses throne; A5 exceeds cushion), relationship 4 (B offers comfort to both), heightening 5 (A5 sacrifices sleep), specificity 4 (A1 establishes courtly seating), brevity/wit 4 (A5 follows competitive hospitality); total 93. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The bed may be offstage, leaving the last demonstration as a sincere commitment rather than an immediate action.
records.writerReservation: A5 offers future demonstrations rather than requiring enacted movement; the spoken commitments must feel immediate and sincere.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a competes through comfort sacrifices; b competes through increasingly conspicuous written proof.

beats.text: Wear this ribbon before dinner. It prevents emotional lightning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no such thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Doubt attracts it. You'll need a second ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My hands are covered. I can't hold a fork.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Metal conducts resentment. I'll feed you with a wooden spoon, after we insulate your opinions.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 invents ribbon protection and A3 turns doubt into exposure, but A5 treats B4's objection as completion rather than another need for protection.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's disbelief to add a ribbon; A5 acknowledges B4's ribbon coverage but adds no consequence.

relationship.evidence: B2 doubts the hazard and B4 objects to excess, but A5 gives B no changed practical situation.

heightening.evidence: A5 names a safe skepticism level instead of elaborating the precautions beyond A3's second ribbon.

specificity.evidence: A1's ribbons and emotional lightning are immediately playable, though there is no ordinary activity at stake.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 efficiently converts doubt into risk; A5's safe skepticism is coherent but abstract.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 makes doubt require another ribbon; A5 turns impaired eating into a reason for controlled feeding and opinion insulation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's denial directly causes A3's extra protection; B4's fork problem causes A5's wooden spoon, though two ribbons becoming covered hands is compressed.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants to eat independently; A5 sincerely offers help that increases A's control over B's meal and speech.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands wearing protection into being fed and having opinions insulated, using B4's practical objection as justification.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes dinner and a ribbon; B4 and A5 supply playable utensils, with some ambiguity about how the hands became covered.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Doubt attracts it' is efficient; A5's metal/resentment explanation earns the spoon but adds several ideas at once.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 denies the hazard; A3 declares denial an attractor and increases protection.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 cannot hold a fork; A5 identifies metal as another danger and takes over feeding with wood.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A converts each objection into evidence that B requires more impossible safeguards and more supervision.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves from protective clothing into bodily assistance and protection against B's own opinions.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A gains control by prescribing impossible protection and treating resistance or inconvenience as evidence that still more precautions are necessary.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary overprotectiveness exaggerates real hazards; this card invents impossible protective relationships and uses objections to extend control.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 makes doubt attract lightning, and revised A5 makes B4's fork difficulty justify supervised feeding and insulated opinions.

records.recommendedEdit: Added dinner as a natural purpose and made B4's inconvenience specific. A5 now uses the fork objection to extend both protection and A's authority. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3/A5 convert objections into precautions), logic 5 (A3 uses doubt; A5 uses metal cutlery), relationship 4 (B wants to eat independently), heightening 5 (A5 takes over feeding), specificity 5 (dinner, fork and spoon connect), brevity/wit 4 (conducting resentment develops emotional lightning); total 95. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The coverage produced by two ribbons is not clearly established, and the final opinion precaution is less directly tied to the fork.
records.writerReservation: A5's final opinion insulation is abstract; the concrete feeding takeover carries the playable escalation.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a makes protection physically dependent and intimate; b controls access to information by treating future conditions as present hazards.

cards.title: Safety Through Nonsense
cards.instruction: Take control through elaborate impossible precautions, treating every objection as another reason the people present need protection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Helmet on before reading the prophecy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a piece of paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: About tomorrow. We haven't inspected tomorrow for falling objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It predicts sunshine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then add protective glasses. Precautions are working.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Helmet on before reading the prophecy. We haven't inspected tomorrow for falling objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's one sentence. I just want to know if the picnic's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short prophecies concentrate the future. Read it through this oven glove.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It predicts sunshine. Surely that's safe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unfiltered future sunlight. Close the glove. Nobody reads another word until I've put sunscreen on tomorrow.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 invents exposure to tomorrow, but A1's helmet and A5's glasses remain simple ordinary equipment rather than elaborate impossible precautions.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's paper objection through future contents; A5 uses B4's sunshine to add glasses.

relationship.evidence: B2 minimizes the object and B4 offers reassuring contents, though the purpose of reading is undeveloped.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds another item, but sunshine makes protective glasses relatively reasonable and weakens escalation.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies prophecy reading and a helmet; B4 provides a concrete prediction.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's uninspected tomorrow follows A's reasoning, while A5's 'working' claim is less clearly justified.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 treats a short prophecy as concentrated danger; A5 treats reassuring sunshine as exposure requiring sunscreen on tomorrow.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's one-sentence objection generates A3's concentration theory; B4's sunshine forecast generates A5's sunlight precaution.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants a picnic decision and B4 offers reassurance; A5 imposes a protective condition that obstructs access to the answer.

heightening.evidence: A5 progresses from shielding the reader with equipment to requiring protection applied to tomorrow itself.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes prophecy reading with a helmet; A3's oven glove is concrete, although reading 'through' it is physically ambiguous.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's concentrated future follows the sentence length; A5's sunscreen follows the sunshine, keeping both absurdities earned.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 argues that one sentence is harmless; A3 makes brevity a concentration hazard requiring another safeguard.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 cites sunshine as safe; A5 interprets that exact forecast as unfiltered exposure and requires future sunscreen.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A takes charge through increasingly impossible precautions and treats reassurance as further evidence of danger.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 expands protection from present reading equipment to the future itself; the reading ban is a negotiable in-scene obstacle, not a prescribed ending.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A controls access to a prophecy through impossible safety procedures and converts each reassurance into a new exposure requiring protection.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Sensible preparation for forecast weather would protect people at the picnic; A instead treats reading future information as direct physical exposure.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 claims a short text concentrates the future, and A5 requires sunscreen on tomorrow itself after B4's reassurance.

records.recommendedEdit: Added a picnic decision and replaced ordinary sunglasses with precautions directed at future information itself. B2's short sentence causes concentration risk; B4's sunshine causes A5's impossible screening requirement. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3/A5 invent protective causation), logic 5 (length and sunshine each cause the next restriction), relationship 4 (B needs a picnic answer), heightening 5 (A5 suspends reading for an impossible precaution), specificity 4 (glove and prophecy support play), brevity/wit 4 (sunscreen follows the claimed sunlight hazard); total 93. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. The oven-glove reading method needs actor interpretation, and A5's prohibition should remain an obstacle B can challenge.
records.writerReservation: A5 imposes a character-level obstacle, not a fixed scene ending; B can still bargain over or challenge the precaution.
records.alternativeComparison: Compared with a's takeover of eating, b escalates the scale of protection while keeping B's picnic-information goal active.
